turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hello there! How's your day treating you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Petrol's so expensive now. I'm retired and I want to squeeze every mile out of a tank.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: There's quite a lot you can do. Smooth driving is the biggest one, accelerating gently and anticipating stops so you brake less.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? Our kitten is about to graduate to a proper litter tray and I can't pick a litter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There are quite a few choices and they're all a bit complicated, so this might take me a while.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The clumping clay one is cheap and easy to scoop, but it's dusty and gets tracked everywhere.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Pine pellets smell nice and are biodegradable, though some cats hate the feel under their paws.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And silica crystals soak up smells really well, but they're expensive and crunchy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, that's all of them, Moshi. Which one grabs you?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Kittens are often fine with clumping clay since it feels like sand. The pine pellets are nice for the planet, but try a small bag first in case she refuses it. Crystals are great at smells, just pricey for a messy kitten.
